q: The Mañé-Sad-Sullivan theorem on holomorphic families: for a holomorphic family {f_λ} of rational maps (λ ∈ D), the Julia set J(f_λ) moves continuously (holomorphically) for λ outside the bifurcation locus. More precisely:
opts: J(f_λ) is always the same set
In the stable set {λ : f_λ is stable (J moves analytically)}, there is a holomorphic motion h: D × J(f₀) → ℂ with h(λ,·) a conjugacy on J
J(f_λ) is compact for all λ
exp: Mañé-Sad-Sullivan (MSS) theorem: stable maps form an open dense set in 1-parameter families (Sullivan, and separately MSS). In the stable component, J moves by a holomorphic motion — a quasiconformal map h_λ: J₀ → J_λ depending holomorphically on λ. The λ-lemma extends this to a quasiconformal conjugacy.
